newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: AWB Report-Prices fall as crop conditions improve.
newsitem.headline: AWB Report-Prices fall as crop conditions improve.

text.p: Australia's wheat market continued to be weather-driven with the Sydney Futures Exchange affected by the U.S. market, the Australian Wheat Board (AWB) said on Friday.

An improved U.S. Hard Red Winter wheat condition report, excellent corn plantings and rain in some parts of eastern Australia and Europe saw prices fall over ther week, it said in its weekly grain market report.
The AWB's national indicator price finished last week down A$3.00 a tonne to A$188.00 fob.
Some parts of the Mallee in Victoria, northern South Australia and southern New South Wales still waited for rain, it said.
Improving U.S. and international crop reports and weather conditions saw a reasonable amount of old crop sales domestically, it said.
The pool price for Australian Standard White remained at A$203.00 a tonne fob.

Internationally, prices fell during the week with wheat prices volatile as world weather patterns remain the short-term driving force. Prices were lower early in the week on improved weather forecasts for Europe and U.S. winter wheat regions.
The lack of significant new crop demand particularly for soft red winter wheat also contributed to further declines in Chicago.
However, later in the week the wheat market firmed on uncertainty about possible negative weather producing lower world wheat.
Overall world wheat prospects improved from a week ago. Rains in Europe and Australia and improving U.S. crop conditions contributed to the fall, it said.
USDA crop estimates on May 13 should provide a clearer benchmark for the market, it said.
